items.caution: Vanessa O’Rourke is wanted for allegedly fraudulently representing to her family and friends that she had been diagnosed with a terminal form of brain cancer known as a glioblastoma, and told them she needed money to aid in her medical treatment and to support her while she was ill.  Between October of 2015 and July of 2016, O'Rourke further represented to family and friends that she needed to travel to Australia to participate in an experimental treatment for her purported cancer.  Through her false and fraudulent pretenses, her family and others provided money and support.  In or around April of 2016, O'Rourke traveled to Australia, where she engaged in a variety of leisure activities and did not receive any medical treatment.  Upon her return to the United States, O'Rourke enlisted her friends and family to organize two fundraisers on her behalf.  A webpage was established and a benefit event held at a local restaurant in Pennsylvania, both resulting in numerous people providing donations for her purported cancer treatment.  O'Rourke utilized those funds to travel to Australia again in or around 2016, where she again engaged in various leisure activities and received no medical treatment for her nonexistent illness.  O'Rourke was indicted on 15 counts of wire fraud in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Pennsylvania on May 3, 2018, and a federal warrant was issued for her arrest.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation's Phoenix Field Office is asking for the public’s assistance in solving the murders of Lila Harrison and Guy Sabori in the Gila River Indian Community in Arizona. 

 

Early in the morning of July 25, 2020, Guy Sabori was driving eastbound along Goodyear Road with Lila Harrison and another passenger on the Gila River Indian Community south of Chandler, Arizona.  At approximately 2:48 a.m., Sabori came to a stop at Goodyear Road at the intersection with Highway 587.  Sabori paused as he was approached by a black pickup truck driving southbound on Highway 587.  The truck slowed, turned onto Goodyear Road, and pulled next to Sabori’s vehicle.  Unknown occupants of the truck then shot several rounds into Sabori’s vehicle, striking and killing Sabori and Harrison, while also hurting the third passenger. The truck continued westbound along Goodyear Road where its occupants were believed to have been involved in another shooting where two additional individuals suffered gunshot wounds in the Snaketown neighborhood approximately ten minutes after Sabori and Harrison were killed.

The suspect is described as a male, possible White or Hispanic, approximately 5'6" with a thin build.  He was wearing a black riot-style helmet, blue goggles, a black balaclava mask, and a dark-colored trench coat with high fluorescent yellow sides and the words "SECURITY Here to assist you" written in yellow fluorescent letters on the back.  The front of the jacket had the numbers #1759 written on the left chest area.  The suspect was also wearing black pants, black tennis shoes or boots, black gloves, and may have worn a TAC-style vest underneath the trench coat.

On July 5, 2015, Crystal Rogers was reported missing by her mother, after she had not been seen or heard from since the evening of July 3, 2015. The same day Rogers was reported missing, her car was found abandoned with a flat tire at mile marker 14 on the Bluegrass Parkway in Bardstown, Kentucky.  Rogers' keys, phone, and purse were still inside her red Chevrolet Impala.  Rogers was the mother of five children and was not known to go anywhere without her children. 

 

In July of 2025, an individual was found guilty by a jury for the murder of Crystal Rogers.  The FBI continues to seek information from the public that would assist in locating her remains.

 

On November 19, 2016, Rogers' father Tommy Ballard was shot and killed on family property near Bluegrass Parkway in Bardstown, Kentucky.

items.details: Gholamhossein Mohammadnia, an official of Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS), is wanted for questioning based on his alleged involvement in the abduction, detention, and probable death of retired FBI Special Agent Robert A. Levinson travelled to Kish Island, Iran, on March 8, 2007, and has not been publicly seen or heard from since his disappearance the following day. items.details: On July 10, 2012, Paige Moore was reportedly last seen by family members at approximately 1 a.m., in her residence in Broken Arrow, Oklahoma. She was last seen wearing a gray GooGoo Dolls long-sleeved t-shirt, red polka-dotted boxer shorts, and red slippers size 7-9. Moore has multiple facial piercing and a tattoo (unconfirmed location). It has been determined that a 2002 dark green Chevrolet Tracker, Oklahoma license plate 931KSW, may have been involved in her disappearance.
items.age_range: 17 years old (at the time of disappearance)
items.title: PAIGE SUMMER MOORE - BROKEN ARROW, OKLAHOMA

items.details: On July 16, 2020, Ronald Green and Clifton “Casey” Emmert were shot and killed outside of Cumberland Marketplace in Smyrna, Georgia. The victims were sitting inside of a green 1999 Mercury Grand Marquis at the time of the shooting.  The suspect is described as a thinly built Black male with short dreads in a twist-style. He was wearing a red hooded sweatshirt/hoodie with white stripes, black fitted jeans, a medical face mask, and red/white sneakers. The suspect fled in a dark grey, newer model Toyota Camry with a “tag applied for” license plate.
items.title: RONALD GREEN AND CLIFTON EMMERT - SMYRNA, GEORGIA

items.details: On September 24, 1973, Ruth Brenneman was last seen being dropped off at William Penn High School in York, Pennsylvania. She failed to return home that evening and was reported missing. Then, on October 10, 1973, she was found deceased in Lebanon County, Pennsylvania, on Ft. Indiantown Gap, a military property. Investigators are asking anyone who may have known Brenneman at the time of her disappearance or have any knowledge of her death to please reach out.
items.title: RUTH BRENNEMAN - YORK, PENNSYLVANIA

items.details: On May 6, 2025, William Dean Willis was reported missing by his family. Willis has not been seen or heard from since the early evening of May 5, 2025. All of his belongings were left behind at his residence.  Willis was last seen wearing a black trench coat and black jeans. He has a floral tattoo on his right forearm. He also has piercings in both of his ears (gauged), septum, and left lower lip, and is known to wear a black cross around his neck. Willis has a history of heroin use and mental illness. He is known to frequent areas of 6th and 8th Streets in North Camden as well as Franklinville and Manua in New Jersey.
